definitions.BOAT: A craft used for transportation of goods, fishing, racing, recreational cruising, or military use on or in the water, propelled by oars or outboard motor or inboard motor or by wind.
definitions.SHIP: A water-borne vessel generally larger than a boat.
definitions.SAIL: A piece of fabric spread to catch the wind and propel a vessel.
definitions.MAST: A tall upright post on a ship or boat, carrying sails.
definitions.DECK: A flat covered surface that forms a floor on a ship.
definitions.HULL: The watertight body of a ship or boat.
definitions.PORT: The left side of a ship when facing forward.
definitions.BOW: The front end of a ship.
definitions.RIVER: A large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea.
definitions.LAKE: A small stream of running water; a channel for water; a drain.
definitions.OCEAN: One of the large bodies of water separating the continents.
definitions.WAVE: To move back and forth repeatedly and somewhat loosely.
definitions.TIDE: The periodic change of the sea level, particularly when caused by the gravitational influence of the sun and the moon.
definitions.SURF: Waves that break on an ocean shoreline.
definitions.FISH: A cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills.
definitions.GULL: A seabird of the genus Larus or of the family Laridae.
definitions.YACHT: A sailboat or motorboat used for cruising or racing.
definitions.CANOE: A lightweight narrow boat, typically pointed at both ends, propelled by paddles.
definitions.KAYAK: A small, narrow watercraft propelled by a double-bladed paddle.
definitions.RAFT: A flat buoyant structure of timber, barrels, or other materials used for transport.
definitions.DOCK: A platform or structure extending into the water for vessels to tie up.
definitions.PIER: A platform supported on pillars, leading out into the water.
definitions.BUOY: An anchored float serving as a navigation mark or warning.
definitions.KNOT: A unit of speed equal to one geographical mile per hour.
definitions.ANCHOR: A heavy metal device cast overboard to keep a vessel in place.
definitions.CREW: The group of people who work on and operate a ship or boat.
definitions.WATER: A substance (of molecular formula H₂O) found at room temperature and pressure as a clear liquid.
definitions.BEACH: The shore of a body of water, especially when sandy or pebbly.
definitions.SAND: Rock that is ground more finely than gravel, but is not as fine as silt (more formally, see grain sizes chart), forming beaches and deserts and also used in construction.
definitions.SHELL: A hard external covering of an animal.
definitions.SHORE: Land adjoining a non-flowing body of water, such as an ocean, lake or pond.
definitions.COAST: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
definitions.SEA: A large body of salt water.
definitions.HOOK: A rod bent into a curved shape, typically with one end free and the other end secured to a rope or other attachment.
definitions.NET: A figure made up of a large number of straight lines or curves,which are connected at certain points and related to each other bysome specified law.
definitions.BAIT: Any substance, especially food, used in catching fish, or other animals, by alluring them to a hook, snare, trap, or net.
definitions.OAR: A type of lever used to propel a boat, having a flat blade at one end and a handle at the other, and pivoted in a rowlock atop the gunwale, whereby a rower seated in the boat and pulling the handle can pass the blade through the water by repeated strokes against the water's resistance, thus moving the boat .
definitions.ROAM: To wander or travel freely and with no specific destination.
definitions.FLOW: A movement in people or things with a particular way in large numbers or amounts.
definitions.CABIN: A small dwelling characteristic of the frontier, especially when built from logs with simple tools and not constructed by professional builders, but by those who meant to live in it.
definitions.PADDLE: A two-handed, single-bladed oar used to propel a canoe or a small boat.
definitions.FERRY: A ship used to transport people, smaller vehicles and goods from one port to another, usually on a regular schedule.
definitions.BARGE: A large flat-bottomed towed or self-propelled boat used mainly for river and canal transport of heavy goods or bulk cargo.
definitions.STREAM: A small, narrow river of flowing water.
definitions.CREEK: A small inlet or bay, often saltwater, narrower and extending farther into the land than a cove; a recess in the shore of the sea, or of a river; the inner part of a port that is used as a dock for small boats.
definitions.BROOK: To use; enjoy; have the full employment of.
definitions.POND: An inland body of standing water, either natural or man-made, that is smaller than a lake.
definitions.CORAL: A hard substance made of the limestone skeletons of marine polyps.
definitions.REEF: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
definitions.FLOAT: A buoyant device used to support something in water or another liquid.
definitions.DRIFT: (physical) Movement; that which moves or is moved.
definitions.SPRAY: A fine, gentle, dispersed mist of liquid.
definitions.MIST: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air.
definitions.DEEP: (with "the") The deep part of a lake, sea, etc.
definitions.BLUE: The colour of the clear sky or the deep sea, between green and violet in the visible spectrum, and one of the primary additive colours for transmitted light; the colour obtained by subtracting red and green from white light using magenta and cyan filters; or any colour resembling this.
definitions.SALT: A common substance, chemically consisting mainly of sodium chloride (NaCl), used extensively as a condiment and preservative.
definitions.CARGO: Freight carried by a ship, aircraft, or motor vehicle.
definitions.STERN: The back or rear end of a ship.
definitions.RIG: The rigging of a sailing ship or other such craft.
definitions.ROPE: Thick strings, yarn, monofilaments, metal wires, or strands of other cordage that are twisted together to form a stronger line.
definitions.LINE: A path through two or more points (compare ‘segment’); a continuous mark, including as made by a pen; any path, curved or straight.
definitions.NAVY: A country's entire sea force, including ships and personnel.
definitions.MARINE: A soldier, normally a member of a marine corps, trained to serve on board or from a ship.
definitions.VALVE: A device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid through a pipe.
definitions.PUMP: A device for moving or compressing a liquid or gas.
definitions.WHARF: A man-made landing place for ships on a shore or river bank.
definitions.JETTY: A structure of wood or stone extended into the sea to influence the current or tide, or to protect a harbor or beach.
definitions.QUAY: A stone or concrete structure on navigable water used for loading and unloading vessels; a wharf.
definitions.LOCK: Something used for fastening, which can only be opened with a key or combination.
definitions.CANAL: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
definitions.BASIN: A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall.
definitions.COVE: A hollow in a rock; a cave or cavern.
definitions.GULF: A hollow place in the earth; an abyss; a deep chasm or basin.
definitions.STRAIT: A narrow channel of water connecting two larger bodies of water.
definitions.CHANNEL: The physical confine of a river or slough, consisting of a bed and banks.
definitions.FJORD: A long, narrow, deep inlet between cliffs.
definitions.MARSH: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass.
definitions.SWAMP: A piece of wet, spongy land; low ground saturated with water; soft, wet ground which may have a growth of certain kinds of trees, but is unfit for agricultural or pastoral purposes.
definitions.DELTA: The fourth letter of the modern Greek alphabet Δ, δ.
definitions.LAGOON: A shallow body of water separated from deeper sea by a bar.
definitions.ISLE: A wing of a building, notably in a church separated from the nave proper by piers.
definitions.SHOAL: A sandbank or sandbar creating a shallow.
definitions.BEACON: A signal fire to notify of the approach of an enemy, or to give any notice, commonly of warning.
definitions.LIGHTHOUSE: A tower or other structure exhibiting a light or lights to warn or guide sailors.
definitions.RUDDER: An underwater vane used to steer a vessel.
definitions.TILLER: A person who tills; a farmer.
definitions.COMPASS: A magnetic or electronic device used to determine the cardinal directions (usually magnetic or true north).
definitions.RADAR: A method of detecting distant objects and determining their position, velocity, or other characteristics by analysis of sent radio waves (usually microwaves) reflected from their surfaces.
definitions.GALLEY: A long, slender ship propelled primarily by oars, whether having masts and sails or not; usually referring to rowed warships used in the Mediterranean from the 16th century until the modern era.
definitions.BUNK: One of a series of berths or beds placed in tiers.
definitions.BILGE: The rounded portion of a ship's hull, forming a transition between the bottom and the sides.
